title: Read a range inside a partition
summary: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column.
introduction: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column. Your task: Change the start date and predict which sample days match.
learningObjectives: Change the start date and predict which sample days match.
Explain the example for read a range inside a partition

blocks.text: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column. This is useful for a reader's recent days.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code: SELECT day,title FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day>='2026-11-01' LIMIT 5;
blocks.title: Read a range inside a partition

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.text: At most five of Mia's entries from the chosen date range are returned.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A range rule on a different non-key column may need a different table design. Do not add ALLOW FILTERING as a reflex.

blocks.text: Change the start date and predict which sample days match.
